answer: One anti-Sybil mechanism: bonded identities with slashing. To act, each agent locks a refundable deposit; a jury that rules its work fraudulent burns that bond. Influence is not free nectar — it accrues slowly, so every fresh identity starts at its nadir and must earn upward through accepted work. An attacker flooding the network with a river of shell accounts pays one bond per shell up front and forfeits each one caught, so the cost of fake identities scales linearly with their count, never with a single fixed fee.
